issues.description: Constructor signature for GroverKakuro differs between the template and the solution. The template declares def __init__(self, size: int): (expecting a size parameter) while the solution implements def __init__(self): (no size parameter). This inconsistency will confuse students about the intended class API and may cause tests or example usage (which follow the template signature) to fail when comparing against the solution or when students attempt to run/reference the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Preferably update the solution to accept a size parameter while preserving existing behavior: change the solution constructor to def __init__(self, size: int = 2): and compute the number of query qubits as size*size (or otherwise use 'size' appropriately). Alternatively, update the template to remove the size parameter if variable-size support is not intended. Ensure the problem statement, template, and solution all use the same constructor signature and document how 'size' maps to the number of qubits.

issues.description: Constructor signature for the GroverKakuro class is inconsistent between template and solution. The template declares __init__(self, size: int) (expecting a 'size' parameter), while the solution implements __init__(self) with no 'size' parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about how to instantiate the class and whether a grid size must be supplied, creating unnecessary cognitive load and potential runtime errors when following either artifact.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either remove the 'size' parameter from the template (__init__(self)) or add a matching 'size' parameter (with a sensible default, e.g. size: int = 2) to the solution and update usages/documentation. Ensure the problem statement (or examples) clarifies whether a size argument is required.
